Mining Type of Mining Other Info: 88.29% of the coal block area is under Forest land, of these, 93.69% is Reserved Forest. Approximately half of the Northern  part of the block is densely Forested. Mining Blasting Other Info:
In Opencast Mining OB will be removed using combination of shovel and dumpers. Blasting in overburden will be done in such a manner that  blast induced ground vibrations will be within the permissible limit as per statute/DGMS circulars and coal will be extracted deploying surface minor. 
In underground Mining Coal will be extracted deploying continues minors, hence blasting may not be required.
Mining External Dumping Remarks: Within mine lease area, partially re-handled for backfilling and part of the external dump will be utilized for making M-sand.
Mining Topsoil Dumping Remarks: Within mine lease area, topsoil will be re-handled and spread over backfilled dump for its restoration.
Mining Quarry Other Info: This area will be converted as water body for future water recharge and public use.
Mining Transportation Mode From Pithead: Coal transportation from pit head to railway siding will be done by tripping trucks through the existing connecting roads.
Mining Transportation Mode Other Info: Coal excavated from Both Opencast and Underground Mine would be brought in the Surface Stock Pile earmarked in the infrastructure area. Since the Coal Block is allocated for commercial mining and open sale, hence the final destination is not determined at this stage of time and the destination may vary time to time.  From the Surface Stock Pile all the coal would be transported by tripping trucks thought existing roads connecting to either of the existing Railway Sidings at Ghunghuti (around 7 Kms) or Bandhwabara (around 9 Kms) located on Katni-Bilaspur Rail line of South East Central Railway and coal loaded in the wagon would be transported to the final consumer destinations by Rail. As per the requirement and location of the destination, some portion of the coal may be transported by existing connecting roads by tripping trucks loaded in surface Stock Piles.

Project Description:
The transmission scheme comprises “Inter-regional (NR-WR) Transmission System
strengthening to relieve the loading of 765 kV Vindhyachal-Varanasi D/C line”. The issues related to high loading of existing 765 kV Vindhyachal–Varanasi D/C line during high NR import were being observed in real-time at the time of high demand in Uttar Pradesh. Due to this high loading of 765 kV Vindhyachal-Varanasi D/C line (under N-1 contingency), violation of WR-NR Available Transfer Capability (ATC) and NR simultaneous import is also being observed in real-time. WR-NR ATC violations in Realtime would lead to situation wherein NR states would not be able to draw further power from Western region. In view of above, comprehensive transmission scheme was evolved to resolve critical loading of 765 kV Vindhyachal-Varanasi D/C line in ‘N-1’ contingency condition as well as for transaction of power in respect of Pump Storage Projects (PSPs) located in Uttar Pradesh (UP).

Project Description:
It is a green field project. Opencast mechanized method of mining will be proposed. Lumps of Bauxite were being transported from pit bottom to surface by dumper. Whenever sorting of Bauxite was required, it was being done manually.  After sorting, beneficiation process will be done. The waste is in the form of lateritic soil which is treated as OB. The massive and hard strata will be loosened by hammering. Excavated bauxite from the bench will be carried through truck/dumper manually. The individual bench faces will be kept nearly vertical (80° - 85°) while the overall pit slope will be approx. 45°. The presently explored area for the mineralization of Bauxite is 102.00 hectares.
